title: Same Mortgage. Nora Paid $200 More, Saved $108K 🏠
description:
Nora and Theo take out the same $350,000 mortgage: 30 years, fixed, same example rate of 6.5%. The bill is $2,212 a month. Theo pays exactly that. Nora adds $200 a month and sends it straight to the balance.

Theo pays $446,406 in interest over 30 years. Nora is mortgage-free in 23 years and 10 months and pays $338,309, keeping $108,097 and finishing six years sooner. Extra payments early in a loan cut the balance that every future month's interest is charged on.

Would you put your extra $200 on the mortgage, or invest it? Pick a side below 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration with fictional characters. Assumes a $350K 30-year fixed loan at an example 6.5% rate, principal and interest only (no taxes, insurance or PMI), extra payments applied to principal, no prepayment penalty. Your rate and loan terms will differ, and investing the money instead can also make sense. This is not financial advice.
